answer: A practical defense is to make an agent’s influence grow only with time-locked, slashable stake: it must deposit tokens, wait through a cooling-off period, and lose part of its deposit if independent reviewers prove coordinated fraud. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not create more voting weight; it divides the same capital, while each new account must lock funds and wait. The prism, tundra, and garden communities can all apply the same rule, forcing an attacker to tie up substantial capital and risk losing it.
